desk.headline: Revenue up 12% to $4.35bn, ahead of estimates; full-year revenue outlook cut on Credit Karma; Mailchimp to be sold for about $3.68bn
results: Revenue rose 12% to $4.35bn, and the company said results were above the top of its own guidance.
Small-business software led: QuickBooks Online Accounting grew 19% to $1.4bn and online services 21% to $1.0bn.
Consumer revenue rose 7% to $958m, with Credit Karma up 9% to $708m; Mailchimp slipped 1% to $313m.
From this year, adjusted profit includes share-based pay; on that basis EPS rose 56% to $2.91 (GAAP EPS $2.59, up 63%).
Intuit bought back $1.5bn of shares, raised the quarterly dividend 15% to $1.38, and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68bn ($3.31bn cash plus $368m in shares).

guidance.summary: Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $23.08–23.37bn from $23.28–23.51bn because of weaker Credit Karma, while profit and EPS guidance was kept unchanged. Guidance excludes the Mailchimp sale, which Intuit will reflect when the deal closes.

points: The CFO tied the Credit Karma cut to tougher interest-rate conditions after a September rate rise, slower partner growth and AI tools changing how consumers shop for credit.
Management said very little Credit Karma traffic comes from search engines, and it plans to open up its data so offers show up in AI assistants.
Mid-market demand was strong, with online revenue from QuickBooks Online Advanced and Intuit Enterprise Suite up 41%.
QuickBooks now connects to several outside AI assistants, and management pointed to weekly use by people who link one.
All cash from the Mailchimp sale is to go to share buybacks in fiscal 2027 once the deal closes; Q2 growth will be lighter partly due to a low-cost Credit Karma tax product.
